summary: Orbital Sweeper is an interactive space traffic management and Active Debris Removal (ADR) intelligence platform. Addressing The Earth Information Jukebox challenge, it transforms complex orbital datasets into an accessible, interactive visual experience that reveals how space debris in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) directly threatens the Earth-observing, weather, and communication satellites we rely on every day. With over 34,000 tracked objects and 14,000+ pieces of debris creating critical collision risks (Kessler Syndrome), passive data is not enough. Using NASA's ORDEM 3.2 debris model and real Space-Track TLE catalogs, Orbital Sweeper visualizes high-risk congestion zones (700–1,000 km) and calculates the most fuel-efficient (Delta-v) trajectories to capture and safely de-orbit hazardous debris—protecting vital Earth information infrastructure and ensuring a sustainable orbital environment.
details:
What It Does: Orbital Sweeper is an interactive data visualization and Active Debris Removal (ADR) mission-planning platform built to make orbital safety data intuitive and actionable. Addressing The Earth Information Jukebox challenge, it translates complex astrodynamics and NASA space debris datasets into a clear, interactive interface that demonstrates how orbital congestion in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) jeopardizes critical Earth-monitoring, meteorological, and telecommunications satellites.

How It Works & Key Features:

  1. LEO Traffic Map: A live interactive visualization displaying the real-time orbital distribution of active Earth-serving satellites versus tracked space debris across Low Earth Orbit.
  2. Congestion Profile: An analytical risk-assessment chart illustrating collision probability densities across altitudes, highlighting critical danger zones heavily concentrated between 700 km and 1,000 km.
  3. Objects in Focus: A curated, searchable catalog of hazardous space objects indexed by their official NORAD ID, altitude, velocity, and collision risk score.
  4. Cleanup Path Planner: An interactive simulation tool where users select a high-risk debris target—such as Fengyun 1C at 865 km altitude or Cosmos 2251 fragments—and explore optimal cleanup trajectories. The system calculates orbital transfer requirements and the minimum propellant expenditure (Delta-v) needed to capture the target and execute a controlled de-orbit.

Benefits & Impact: By turning raw orbital tracking catalogs into an accessible decision-making and educational tool, Orbital Sweeper raises awareness and reduces the projected propellant cost and operational complexity of ADR missions. Protecting operational satellites in LEO directly safeguards essential Earth-dependent services—including climate and weather monitoring, GPS navigation, and global communications—worth billions of dollars, preventing cascading collisions (Kessler Syndrome).

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

  • Frontend & Visualization: React, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, Three.js / WebGL for interactive 3D orbital mapping, and Chart.js for congestion analytics.
  • Backend & Orbital Mechanics: Python, NumPy, SciPy, and SGP4 orbital propagation libraries for TLE parsing and Delta-v orbital transfer calculations.
